about: The paper-trade bodies the browser sends WITH a TradePlan reference (Phase 2.1). Generated from the backend's own builders; backend/tests/test_trade_plan_contract.py sends them through the real route and checks the plans are the ones the backend builds, and the Playwright specs assert the browser sends exactly these bodies. cash: MOCK — not real data (the RELIANCE-like world of backend/tests/test_strategy_plan.py). fno: the REAL 2026-10-21 staging capture desk-strategy-top.json, its plan built by regime_fit.attach_trade_plans.

selection.source: AI scanner (watchlist + picks), end of day
selection.rule: The scanner's merged list (watchlist and picks, picks win for entry, stop and target), ranked by the scanner's score, then only stocks that pass the scan snapshot's eligibility gates (a price and previous close, 20-session traded value, reference data, series EQ or BE, not an ETF, price band at least 10%, not at its band limit, and traded value of at least Rs 10 crore a day); the top N that pass. When the snapshot cannot be read, the scanner's own liquid flag (the same crore gate on its 20-session average) is the only gate.
selection.excluded_note: Only setups ranked above the last selected one are listed.

ideas_response.ranking_note: Ideas keep the scanner's rank: its rules-based score, which is a rank and not a probability. Within an idea, `preferred` is the viable strategy with the best net reward : risk at the conservative level. Reward : risk of a hedged or income structure (a long put or a short call changes the loss at the stop) is not comparable with an unhedged one: read max loss and capital at risk beside it. No probability and no composite score is produced. With Chartink included, ideas the AI scanner lists come first, ranked by its score; stocks only Chartink listed follow them, ranked by the number of your enabled bullish Chartink scans that listed them and then by traded value. A scan count is not a probability and not a score; your Chartink scans are your own screens and have not been validated.

entry.logic: Last close 1200 (nidp.prices_eod_adjusted close, 2026-10-19); a close above the trigger on volume confirms it

stop.rationale: the scanner's stop (1160): 1.5 x ATR(14) below 1195 (ATR 23.33)
stop.invalidation: the thesis is wrong if price closes beyond this level

targets.name: conservative
targets.rule: 1 x ATR(14) (no resistance at least 0.5 x ATR away)

costs.basis: a round trip of 1 unit(s) from the entry to the stop
excluded: gap slippage beyond the cost card's slippage
costs.gap_risk: A stop is a level, not a guaranteed price: a session that opens through the stop is filled at that open (the desk's fill model), which can be worse than the stop. The cost estimate's slippage (0.05% a side) covers the spread, not a gap.

time.basis: the setup's maximum horizon in sessions, else the plan's horizon

ideas.capital_at_risk_basis: worst net loss over all prices, every leg charged entry and exit costs; null when the loss is unbounded
ideas.reward_risk_basis: net P&L at the chain's expected move over the capital at risk; the theoretical figure measures the payoff at an underlying price of zero and is shown for reference only

caveats: Margin is not the maximum loss.

universe.source: the AI scanner's merged setup list (services/strategy_plan/selection.select_opportunities)

cash.ranking: Ideas keep the scanner's rank: its rules-based score, which is a rank and not a probability. Within an idea, `preferred` is the viable strategy with the best net reward : risk at the conservative level. Reward : risk of a hedged or income structure (a long put or a short call changes the loss at the stop) is not comparable with an unhedged one: read max loss and capital at risk beside it. No probability and no composite score is produced. With Chartink included, ideas the AI scanner lists come first, ranked by its score; stocks only Chartink listed follow them, ranked by the number of your enabled bullish Chartink scans that listed them and then by traded value. A scan count is not a probability and not a score; your Chartink scans are your own screens and have not been validated.

top_response.ranking_note: Ranked by fit to the market regime measured on the dates shown and by the live end-of-day option chain, then by reward : risk. This is not a forecast, not a probability, and not a ranking by past performance: no strategy performance is recorded for options in this system. Nothing here is an instruction to trade and nothing is sent to a broker.
top_response.ranking_note_cash: The cash class is NOT ranked by regime fit: it is the desk's existing 'From AI opportunities' answer, kept unchanged, so it carries the scanner's own evidence rank and its ideas have no fit score. The two are shown side by side rather than merged into one ranking.
gaps: No IV percentile or IV rank: no option-implied-volatility history is stored, so 'rich' and 'cheap' volatility use India VIX against the desk-regime threshold (desk-regime-v1 vix_high), not a percentile of this underlying's own IV.
No performance ranking: the only realised records are three manual cash backtests (public.strategy_trades); there is no options performance history, so no idea here can be ranked by what it earned.
End of day only: the chain is the NSE F&O bhavcopy close. There is no intraday option data.
An index has no cash leg: NIFTY and BANKNIFTY cannot be held, so covered calls, protective puts and collars are offered for stocks only.
